claims.statement: Incoming201 tag2 sets session u.a; tag1 supplies the challenge. Client constructs202 tag1 as Java String.hashCode of challenge + saved password.toLowerCase(). This source verifies the client computation, not historical server acceptance or password policy.

The synchronized counter is incremented before wire transaction assignment; ordinary queued requests and generated pings use (short)(counter %32767 +1). This is not an unrestricted unsigned16-bit counter.

The scheduler compares idle time strictly greater than60000ms for TCP or5000ms for HTTP. TCP queues2 with field1 int1 if no ping is pending; an outstanding ping invokes reconnect. HTTP uses null-request GET polling. These are client scheduling thresholds, not server guarantees.

The main HTTP timer is120s before authenticated flag and30s afterwards. The separate private HTTP/HTTPS helper schedules its own30s timeout. Connection-test wait is45s before authentication/60s after; request400 gets a120s wait in the scheduler.
Enabled flagq plus HTTP mode and existing h queue route922 through that separate queue. It is conditional client behavior, not an unconditional second HTTP API.
Cookie lookup chooses a stored key by substring matching the extracted host; it does not implement standard domain/path scoping. Any URL containing img.mig33.com gets an empty cookie string.

Set-Cookie handling splits semicolon components, then key/value at the first equals sign, storing attributes as ordinary entries. The approximate1024-byte budget mixes byte sizing with character slicing. No browser-equivalent expiry/security semantics are established.

claims.statement: Marker2, signed-short opcode, signed-short transaction, signed-int body length; fields have signed-short tag, signed-int payload length and raw payload. Java DataInput/DataOutput impose big-endian numeric byte order. No transmitted field-type discriminator exists.

ay stores fields in Hashtable under short tag, so later duplicates replace earlier values and serialization enumeration order is unspecified. Raw wire order must not become an application requirement.

A raw field can be read by several accessors:00010002 gives byte0, short1, int65538 and longnull. Numeric readers consume only their width from the start, ignoring trailing bytes. Mixed accessor use is therefore possible on the same wire bytes.

A locally constructed int field exposes only its matching typed getter, but serialization followed by original decoding produces raw bytes that expose numeric-prefix, text and array reads. Internal object discriminator must not be treated as a wire type code.

Missing fields return null through ay accessors. A present zero-byte raw field returns empty text and empty array; short/int/long return null, but byte access throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Safe clone accessors need not reproduce this malformed-input crash.

Raw text is decoded with UTF-8, with fallback to platform-default constructor only on exception. Strings are not DataOutput.writeUTF strings. The Java21 probe replaces invalid ff with U+FFFD; that runtime observation alone does not prove every historical CLDC malformed-Unicode behavior.

TA serialization writes UTF-8 values with NUL only between values. Original decoding has a stale previous-segment-length loop bound and can drop valid nonempty later entries: a\0b becomes[a]; ab\0cd\0ef becomes[ab,cd]; alice@example.test\0bob becomes[alice@example.test]. The issue is broader than empty-segment handling.

The original parser accepts negative body length as an empty body and can consume a field extending beyond the declared body length. Negative field length throws NegativeArraySizeException; truncation throws EOFException. These are original validation defects, not requirements to weaken the bounded Go codec.

ay.a(byte[]) parses until the input is exhausted and returns null for an empty stream. Two complete concatenated frames become two packets. An invalid marker or trailing truncated frame throws rather than returning a successful prefix batch.

Participant-menu value comes from current selection y.a(y.m), stored in local4. Switch actions100/102/108/1000 use it for gift/profile/SMS/transfer respectively; action106 instead refreshes the roster selection before reading its mobile.
Server conversation-menu prefix gets imType=s.g()&cid=s.e() for private, gcid=s.b for group and roomName=s.b for room. No separator is inserted between prefix and the first key.
Overlay1 appends cid=selected t.a&pres=selected t.j, overlay2 appends gid=selected t.b, other custom menu URLs pass through. Prefix must supply its own initial query separator.

Notification action opens t.u; Read Email opens aj.P; Updates ClickLink passes aj.ac (an av instance) h() result to the page/native bridge. They do not acquire the contact/group-menu suffix automatically.

The HTML renderer defaults form method to get, lowercases supplied method, builds control values in page order and substitutes spaces with%20. get makes action+'?'+body; other methods use a separate body. This verifies client construction, not remotely supplied actions or backend validation.

Normal aj page opening runs y.g(space replacement) on URLs not starting P, then delegates URL and body through bl. The route literals' null bodies therefore express initial GET navigation, not the eventual method of a returned form.
